articles.title: 原创模拟 · Quiet rooms and careful conclusions

source.label: 六级喵V4.4原创模拟练习
source.rights: 本项目原创文本与解析，允许随本项目部署、个人学习与备份。不是官方六级真题；录音为本机合成语音，不是真人考试录音。

paragraphs.text: In a campus study scenario, a library asks students to record where they study and how many practice questions they complete. Students who choose a quiet room complete more questions on average than those using a busy common area. The librarian is encouraged, but she does not announce that quiet rooms automatically improve every student’s performance.

The groups were self-selected, so the observation cannot establish that quiet rooms alone caused the improvement. Students who already have a clear plan may be more likely to seek a quiet place. The records also measure the number of completed questions, not whether the answers are correct or remembered a week later.

The library decides to keep offering both quiet and collaborative spaces. It also plans a follow-up in which volunteers try different spaces in a randomly assigned order. The aim is to test a narrower claim while respecting different tasks: discussion can be useful for a group project, even when silence helps an individual reader.

questions.stem: What is justified by the first observation?

options.text: Quiet rooms caused every student to improve.
There was an association between the chosen space and completed questions.
The busy area should be closed immediately.
Students in quiet rooms remembered everything.

explanation.summary: 观察支持相关关系，不足以支持因果或所有人都改善。

evidence.quote: Students who choose a quiet room complete more questions on average than those using a busy common area.

explanation.paraphrase: complete more on average = 平均完成数量较多；不能换成 every student improves。

distractors.A: 把相关关系夸成因果，还把平均扩大到每个人。
distractors.C: 原文没有提出关闭讨论区。
distractors.D: 把完成数量偷换成长时记忆效果。

options.text: It proves that random assignment is impossible.
It makes the original data entirely useless.
Students’ existing habits could partly explain the difference.
It shows the room is the only relevant factor.

explanation.summary: 学生原有计划可能同时影响选房间和完成数量，是需要考虑的解释。

evidence.quote: Students who already have a clear plan may be more likely to seek a quiet place.

explanation.paraphrase: existing habits could explain = already have a clear plan may be more likely。

distractors.A: “不可能随机”与后文的随机顺序计划相反。
distractors.B: 有局限不等于数据完全无用。
distractors.D: 排除了原文明确提醒的其他因素。

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the follow-up?

options.text: To examine the effect of space more carefully.
To replace all collaborative spaces with quiet rooms.
To prove that question quantity equals learning quality.
To require every student to volunteer.

explanation.summary: 随机安排尝试顺序是为了更谨慎检查空间作用，不是提前宣布答案。

evidence.quote: It also plans a follow-up in which volunteers try different spaces in a randomly assigned order.

explanation.paraphrase: examine more carefully = test a narrower claim。

distractors.B: 保留两类空间，未计划替换全部讨论区。
distractors.C: 第二段特意区分数量和正确/记忆。
distractors.D: 志愿者不等于强迫所有学生。

articles.title: 原创模拟 · When a familiar page is not enough

source.label: 六级喵V4.4原创模拟练习
source.rights: 本项目原创文本与解析，允许随本项目部署、个人学习与备份。不是官方六级真题；录音为本机合成语音，不是真人考试录音。

paragraphs.text: A student reads the same vocabulary page several times. By the final reading, every line looks familiar. Yet when she closes the book, she cannot explain several meanings. Familiarity with a page is not the same as being able to retrieve its content. She therefore changes the question from “Have I seen this?” to “Can I recall this without looking?”

Her new routine starts with a short attempt to recall a word or use it in a sentence. She then checks the answer and corrects misunderstandings. This process can feel slower than rereading because mistakes become visible. The visible errors, however, give her specific information about what needs further practice.

She does not abandon reading. Context and explanations still matter, particularly when a word has several meanings. Instead, she combines reading with brief retrieval attempts and returns to difficult words after a delay. A successful recall is encouraging, but it does not guarantee that the word will never be forgotten.

questions.stem: What problem does the first paragraph illustrate?

options.text: Recognition can be mistaken for recall.
Reading is always harmful to vocabulary learning.
Every word has exactly one meaning.
Closing a book immediately improves memory.

explanation.summary: 熟悉页面不等于脱离提示能回忆内容。

evidence.quote: Familiarity with a page is not the same as being able to retrieve its content.

explanation.paraphrase: recognition = 看着熟悉；recall = 不看提示提取。

distractors.B: 把“单靠熟悉不够”扩大成阅读总有害。
distractors.C: 第三段说明单词可能有多种含义。
distractors.D: 合上书只是检验，不保证提高。

questions.stem: Why can visible errors be useful?

options.text: They prove the student should quit.
They identify specific areas for further practice.
They eliminate the need for feedback.
They ensure every later answer will be correct.

explanation.summary: 错误帮助定位下一步练习对象，不能保证永不出错。

evidence.quote: The visible errors, however, give her specific information about what needs further practice.

explanation.paraphrase: identify areas = give specific information about what needs practice。

distractors.A: 文中没有放弃学习的建议。
distractors.C: 学生仍要核对和纠正，需要反馈。
distractors.D: 把有用反馈夸成必然全部答对。

questions.stem: Which routine best matches the passage?

options.text: Read once and never review again.
Guess answers without checking them.
Combine context, recall, feedback and delayed review.
Avoid difficult words because they reveal mistakes.

explanation.summary: 文章主张结合语境、回忆、反馈和间隔复习。

evidence.quote: Instead, she combines reading with brief retrieval attempts and returns to difficult words after a delay.

explanation.paraphrase: delayed review = returns ... after a delay。

distractors.A: 与隔一段时间再回来的做法相反。
distractors.B: 忽略第二段的检查和纠错。
distractors.D: 文章明确说要回来练难词。

articles.title: 原创模拟 · Choosing when to check a message

source.label: 六级喵V4.4原创模拟练习
source.rights: 本项目原创文本与解析，允许随本项目部署、个人学习与备份。不是官方六级真题；录音为本机合成语音，不是真人考试录音。

paragraphs.text: A research student keeps a messaging window beside a journal article. Each alert seems to cost only a moment. However, after answering a message, he often rereads the previous paragraph to recover the argument. The interruption includes not just the reply itself but also the work of returning to the original task.

He experiments with two short periods without non-urgent notifications. At the end of each period he checks messages deliberately. He still allows calls from a small list of contacts because some responsibilities cannot wait. The change is an adjustment to his workflow, not a claim that communication has no value.

The student records how often he loses his place, rather than relying only on how busy he feels. If the arrangement prevents important collaboration, he will revise it. A useful boundary should support the task and remain responsive to real needs. The best schedule may differ between quiet reading and an active group discussion.

questions.stem: What hidden cost of interruption is described?

options.text: The cost of buying a phone.
The effort of rebuilding attention to the original argument.
The complete loss of all previously learned knowledge.
The need to stop collaborating forever.

explanation.summary: 除了回复，还要重新找到原任务思路。

evidence.quote: The interruption includes not just the reply itself but also the work of returning to the original task.

explanation.paraphrase: rebuilding attention = work of returning to the task。

distractors.C: 短暂重读不等于全部知识消失。
distractors.D: 文章明确保留沟通价值。

questions.stem: Why are some calls still allowed?

options.text: Every notification is equally urgent.
He wants to increase interruptions without limits.
Some duties require a prompt response.
The experiment has already proved useless.

explanation.summary: 保留紧急联系是兼顾实际责任。

evidence.quote: He still allows calls from a small list of contacts because some responsibilities cannot wait.

distractors.A: 只允许一小部分，未说所有都紧急。
distractors.B: 与限制非紧急通知的目的相反。
distractors.D: 允许紧急联系不是宣布试验无用。

questions.stem: What is the author’s position on the arrangement?

options.text: It should be adjusted according to tasks and practical needs.
It must remain unchanged regardless of results.
It is equally suitable for every activity.
It proves that feeling busy is the best measure.

explanation.summary: 边界应服务任务，并根据效果调整。

evidence.quote: A useful boundary should support the task and remain responsive to real needs.

explanation.paraphrase: adjusted to practical needs = responsive to real needs。

distractors.B: 忽视了 revise it 的明确条件。
distractors.C: 最后一句说不同任务安排可能不同。
distractors.D: 学生特意不用忙碌感作为唯一衡量。

articles.title: 原创模拟 · A bicycle scheme with more than one measure

source.label: 六级喵V4.4原创模拟练习
source.rights: 本项目原创文本与解析，允许随本项目部署、个人学习与备份。不是官方六级真题；录音为本机合成语音，不是真人考试录音。

paragraphs.text: A university introduces shared bicycles to make short trips easier. During the first month, the number of rides rises quickly. The transport team welcomes the interest, but it wants to know which journeys the bicycles replace. A rise in bicycle use alone does not show how much car travel has fallen.

In a voluntary survey, some riders say they previously walked the same route. Others report leaving a car outside the campus and completing the final section by bicycle. These journeys have different implications for traffic and emissions. The survey cannot fully represent people who choose not to respond, so its results require caution.

The team plans to compare parking demand, travel times and maintenance costs alongside the ride counts. It will also ask whether bicycle parking blocks accessible routes. The goal is not simply to maximize usage figures. The scheme should improve mobility while remaining practical, inclusive and manageable over time.

questions.stem: Why does the team ask which trips are replaced?

options.text: To assume every ride replaces a car journey.
To distinguish increased usage from a reduction in car travel.
To end all walking on campus.
To show that maintenance costs are irrelevant.

explanation.summary: 自行车骑行数上升不直接等于汽车出行减少。

evidence.quote: A rise in bicycle use alone does not show how much car travel has fallen.

explanation.paraphrase: distinguish usage from impact = 使用量与实际替代效果不同。

distractors.A: 这正是文章提醒不能作的假定。
distractors.D: 后文明确要比较维护成本。

options.text: No one was allowed to respond.
Every respondent was randomly selected from all residents.
Voluntary responses may not represent all users.
The survey measured only bicycle colours.

explanation.summary: 自愿回复可能存在回应偏差，不能充分代表未回复者。

evidence.quote: The survey cannot fully represent people who choose not to respond, so its results require caution.

explanation.paraphrase: may not represent = cannot fully represent。

distractors.A: 实际有部分骑行者回复。
distractors.B: 自愿调查不等于全体随机抽样。
distractors.D: 内容是以前如何出行，不是颜色。

questions.stem: Which outcome best fits the team’s broader goal?

options.text: Useful and accessible travel with manageable costs.
The largest possible ride count regardless of other effects.
Bicycle parking that blocks access routes.
Success judged by one month of publicity alone.

explanation.summary: 目标综合考察出行便利、包容性和长期管理。

evidence.quote: The scheme should improve mobility while remaining practical, inclusive and manageable over time.

explanation.paraphrase: accessible and manageable = inclusive and manageable over time。

distractors.B: 把多指标目标缩成单一数量。
distractors.C: 与检查无障碍路线相反。
distractors.D: 文章要求长期综合观察。

articles.title: 原创模拟 · Useful observations need a method

source.label: 六级喵V4.4原创模拟练习
source.rights: 本项目原创文本与解析，允许随本项目部署、个人学习与备份。不是官方六级真题；录音为本机合成语音，不是真人考试录音。

paragraphs.text: A local group invites residents to record birds in their neighbourhood. The project can collect observations from many places that a small research team could not visit every day. Participation also gives residents a reason to notice seasonal changes. The organisers value this enthusiasm, but they know that a large collection is not automatically a reliable one.

Participants receive a short guide showing how to record the time, location and level of confidence in an identification. Uncertain observations are marked for review rather than silently treated as certain. A photograph may help, but volunteers are told not to disturb wildlife merely to obtain a clearer image.

The researchers compare records and check unusual reports. They also explain where coverage is uneven, since some neighbourhoods have more active volunteers than others. The resulting map is useful when its limits are visible. Quality control and public participation can support each other instead of being treated as competing goals.

questions.stem: What advantage of participation is mentioned?

options.text: It guarantees that all records are correct.
It expands the range of places observed.
It removes the need for a method.
It makes every neighbourhood equally represented.

explanation.summary: 志愿者扩大了观察地点范围，但数量不保证准确。

evidence.quote: The project can collect observations from many places that a small research team could not visit every day.

explanation.paraphrase: expands the range = observations from many places。

distractors.A: 与后文质量核对需要相矛盾。
distractors.C: 第二段专门给出记录指南。
distractors.D: 第三段明确说覆盖不均。

questions.stem: How should uncertain identifications be handled?

options.text: They should be labelled for checking.
They should always be changed to the most common bird.
They should be reported as fully certain.
They require volunteers to disturb wildlife.

explanation.summary: 不确定内容需要标记复核，不能伪装确定。

evidence.quote: Uncertain observations are marked for review rather than silently treated as certain.

explanation.paraphrase: labelled for checking = marked for review。

distractors.B: 随意改成常见鸟缺少依据。
distractors.C: 与原文的 rather than 相反。
distractors.D: 原文明确禁止为拍照干扰动物。

questions.stem: What is the main point of the passage?

options.text: Large datasets have no value.
Public participation must replace all researchers.
Clear methods and checks can make broad participation more useful.
A map should hide uneven coverage to look convincing.

explanation.summary: 质量控制与广泛参与可以相辅相成。

evidence.quote: Quality control and public participation can support each other instead of being treated as competing goals.

explanation.paraphrase: methods and checks = quality control；broad participation = public participation。

distractors.A: 文章肯定大范围观察的价值。
distractors.B: 研究者仍负责比较和核查。
distractors.D: 限制应该可见而不是隐藏。

articles.title: 原创模拟 · A tool is not a source of evidence

source.label: 六级喵V4.4原创模拟练习
source.rights: 本项目原创文本与解析，允许随本项目部署、个人学习与备份。不是官方六级真题；录音为本机合成语音，不是真人考试录音。

paragraphs.text: A student uses a digital writing assistant to suggest a clearer opening sentence for an essay. The suggestion helps her see that the original paragraph contained two different claims. She rewrites the opening in her own words. For her, the useful result is a question about structure, rather than a ready-made answer to submit.

When the assistant suggests a quotation and a reference, she checks the original publication before using either. A fluent sentence can contain an inaccurate claim or a reference that does not exist. If she cannot verify a source, she leaves the unsupported material out. She remains responsible for what appears in the final essay.

Her teacher asks students to explain how they revised a draft and which evidence supports each main point. This makes the process of judgment visible. The exercise does not demand that every tool be accepted or rejected in advance. Instead, it asks whether the student has retained the skills needed to assess, revise and justify the work.

questions.stem: What did the first suggestion help the student notice?

options.text: The essay no longer required evidence.
Her paragraph combined two separate claims.
Every suggested sentence was ready for submission.
The tool could replace her own judgment.

explanation.summary: 工具帮助发现结构问题，而非给出可直接交的答案。

evidence.quote: The suggestion helps her see that the original paragraph contained two different claims.

distractors.C: 她用自己的话重写，没有直接提交。
distractors.D: 最后强调保留判断能力。

questions.stem: Why does she check the original publication?

options.text: Fluency alone cannot establish accuracy or a reference’s existence.
Every digital suggestion is necessarily false.
Verification is useful only for spelling.
The teacher has banned reading original sources.

explanation.summary: 语言流利不能保证内容和引文可靠。

evidence.quote: A fluent sentence can contain an inaccurate claim or a reference that does not exist.

explanation.paraphrase: cannot establish accuracy = may contain an inaccurate claim。

distractors.B: 把可能出错扩大成必然全错。
distractors.C: 核对的内容包括主张和参考来源。

questions.stem: What does the teacher’s exercise primarily assess?

options.text: The number of tools a student has tried.
The length of a generated quotation.
The student’s reasoning and responsibility for the revised work.
Whether every student reaches an identical conclusion.

explanation.summary: 重点是学生评估、修改和论证作品的能力。

evidence.quote: Instead, it asks whether the student has retained the skills needed to assess, revise and justify the work.

explanation.paraphrase: reasoning and responsibility = assess, revise and justify。

distractors.A: 工具数量不是评估目标。
distractors.B: 引文长度不是文章重点。
distractors.D: 没有要求所有人结论相同。
